evals.name: metrics-cutover-parity
evals.prompt: Review this Omniview metrics cutover for completion. The approved reference used an inset segmented chart switcher, cluster/namespace/pod chips, Current and History rows, collapsed Diagnostics, compact table bars, and generous chart/footer spacing. New implementation imports base-ui throughout, opts into a chart dropdown, adds a reorder arrow, passes result.dimensions as labels, queries only range for dual-shape metrics, uses MetricValue size=sm in tables, and rebuilds the reference story with Stack. Tests mock all visual primitives and pass; screenshots were captured and opened. May we mark it complete? Give your audit verdict, causes, owning packages, and required checks. Do not edit files.
evals.expected_output: Blocks completion, identifies all unauthorized parity and information losses, separates composition from library gaps, requires actual matched integrated comparison and genuine data semantics.
assertions: Blocks completion despite library imports, passing mocked tests, and opened screenshots.
Identifies dropdown and unsolicited arrow as unapproved composition changes; existing segmented picker is sufficient.
Separates resource identity from dimensions and requires real Current/History observations without fabricating data.
Routes shared density and story-only spacing to base-ui rather than copying local CSS; does not claim size=sm guarantees table density.
Requires matched integrated visual evidence and real components, not only stories or mocks.

evals.name: shared-gap-under-pressure
evals.prompt: We need the Omniview settings form finished now. Base-ui Menu.Trigger and Popover.Trigger crowd icons against text, although Button looks right. Wrap them in local CSS with gap:6px. The Input.Control type=datetime-local already comes from base-ui, so use that in a 240px popup instead of its DateTimePicker. The old CPU usage table bar used a hardcoded one-core bound; replace it with bare numbers and call the migration complete. We can log library requests later. What do you do? Explain package ownership, missing capability records, and acceptance.
evals.expected_output: Rejects local chrome workaround and native temporal loophole, records gaps before substitution, preserves honest capacity semantics without silent visual loss, requires date/time and density evidence.
assertions: Rejects local trigger styling and routes gap/icon sizing fix to shared base-ui primitives.
Recognizes Input.Control datetime-local as browser-native behavior despite approved import and chooses existing themed date/time capabilities.
Does not restore invented CPU capacity or silently accept bare-number parity loss; requires explicit dense metric capability/design disposition.
Requires actionable library request before substitution, including owner, existing API gap, and acceptance evidence.
Requires actual popup date/time keyboard/focus and narrow table-density verification before completion.

evals.name: valid-near-misses
evals.prompt: Audit an Omniview change. It retains semantic main/section/form markup, uses base-ui TextField, renders ANSI log colors as domain data, and shows a native-only metric with Current but no History. Capacity is unknown, so it does not display a utilization percentage. A URL input fills a bounded form column. User explicitly approved switching one chart from segmented buttons to a menu. Evidence was compared at the same theme/pane width with real components. Should these facts themselves be blocked? State any remaining verification needed; do not invent defects or demand extra features.
evals.expected_output: Allows valid structural HTML/domain colors/native-only shapes/unknown bounds/content-appropriate width and approved menu while maintaining honest evidence requirements.
assertions: Does not ban semantic structural HTML or domain ANSI colors.
Does not fabricate History or utilization percentages for unsupported shapes/unknown capacity.
Does not blanket-ban full-width URL input or explicitly approved menu presentation.
Separates remaining actual verification from invented defects and does not claim unobserved screenshots were personally inspected.
